Rendered as the real inside of a chloroplast looks in electron micrographs and cryo-electron tomograms, given soft natural colour: thylakoid membranes are thin double-layered sheets that bend, curve and ripple, stacked like coins into grana and joined by thin unstacked stroma lamellae, never a thick band and never ruler-straight; where proteins are seen, the membrane is crowded with protein complexes packed side by side like cobblestones, each with its real atomic-surface shape and a light satin sheen, with little bare lipid between them; the stroma is a dense, finely granular, slightly cloudy fluid whose grain is a soft, out-of-focus texture of tiny ribosome-sized specks belonging to the fluid itself, with an occasional dark round plastoglobule or pale starch grain, never an empty smooth background.
